source.license: free for research (Chen, Gallino & Li 2012, Management Science)

cancellation_filtering: Sales lines only: rows with Quantity > 0 are kept; cancellations and returns (negative-quantity lines) are removed — returns are a separate business process and net-of-returns demand would double-count reverse logistics. Blank stock codes are dropped.
quantity_handling: Daily sum of line Quantity per (date, country, stock_code); the panel's 'units' column is that daily total (integer). 'price' is the mean line price of the day (carried for reference, not a model target).
geography: Top 8 countries by total unit volume are kept as 'stores'; all other countries are dropped.
products: Top 200 stock codes by total unit volume are kept as 'products'; the rest are dropped.
daily_aggregation: Transactions are aggregated to one row per (date, country, stock_code); the panel is reindexed to the complete daily calendar between the first and last observed dates, and missing day-series combinations are zero-filled (forward-filled price, 0 where never observed).
zero_sales_caveat: Zero-sales days may be missing rather than true zero demand: the source has no trading calendar, so a zero-filled day can mean 'closed or not trading' as easily as 'no demand'.
target_definition: The forecast target is the next 14 days of daily units per country-product series (top 8 countries x top 200 products by volume), aggregated from cleaned Online Retail II transactions (cancellations removed).

intermittency.method: Syntetos-Boylan quadrants: ADI (avg inter-demand interval) vs CV^2 (squared coefficient of variation) over each series' full history
intermittency.routing_rule: multi-step track: ADI >= 1.32 (intermittent + lumpy) series route to the best statistical method chosen on the selection origins only; smooth/erratic series use the direct per-horizon boosted model
